content.text:
I submitted **index 6** (Bi 0.28, Cu 0.24, V 0.48) as the best composition. At 3.16e-5 A, it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured. The 3-measurement merit budget is used up, and I used none of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 87 | 0.09 / 0.55 / 0.36 (Cu-rich) | 3e-8 |
| 6 | 0.28 / 0.24 / 0.48 (V-rich, Bi-V) | **3.16e-5** |
| 0 | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 (near 1:1 Bi:V) | 1.0e-5 |

- **Cu-rich region:** index 87 came out about 1000x below index 6. MEGNet predicts a very small band gap for Cu₃V₂O₈ (0.09 eV at PBE, 0.67 eV at HSE), which fits a weak result.
- **Bi:V ratio:** index 0, closest to BiVO₄ with the least Cu, came out about 3x lower than index 6. With these three points, extra vanadium looks better than a 1:1 ratio.

**Limitations:**
- **Model receipts:** I couldn't read the phase list because the output was too large and I had no file-reading tool. The only phase ID I could find was mp-504747 (Cu₃V₂O₈), so all the model checks come from that one phase. They pointed away from the Cu-rich region but didn't help pick between the Bi-V candidates.
- **Unmeasured candidates:** after two measurements, the Gaussian-process model's top suggestion was index 9 (Bi 0.34, Cu 0.27, V 0.39), with indices 73, 1 and 74 close behind. I spent the last measurement on index 0 instead, so neighbours of index 6 were never tested. The library's true best may be among them.
